sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match, one word or complete the table).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The mean is obtained by dividing the sum of the items by the ______ of items. (b) Arithmetic mean = Σx ÷ ______.
Fill in the blanks: (a) A weekly consumption of 2.1 kg means a daily consumption of ______ kg. (b) For 10 days it is ______ kg.
State True or False: (a) There are not various measures of central tendency. (b) The arithmetic mean is a measure of central tendency.
questions.answer:
(a) False — there are several (mean, median, mode).
(b) True.

questions.q: Give one word: (a) A single value representative of the whole data. (b) The value assumed in the short-cut method.
Find: (a) The mean of 2, 7, 10, 8, 6, 3, 5, 4, 5, 0. (b) The new mean if an 11th student scoring 5 joins a group of 10 whose mean is 5.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain the concept of central tendency.
questions.answer: Central tendency is the tendency of data to cluster around a central value. The average (e.g. the arithmetic mean) measures it and gives one representative value for the whole data.

questions.q: State the purpose of an average.
questions.answer: An average gives a single value representative of all the items. It sums up large data briefly, makes comparison between groups easy, and helps in framing policy.

or.q: State two functions of an average.
or.answer:
(1) It presents raw data briefly in one representative figure.
(2) It makes comparison between two or more groups easy.

questions.q: Write the short-cut (assumed mean) formula for the arithmetic mean.
questions.answer: X̄ = A + Σfd ÷ N, where A is the assumed mean, d = x − A, f is the frequency and N = Σf. For an individual series, X̄ = A + Σd ÷ N.

questions.q: How is the arithmetic mean obtained?
questions.answer: Add all the items and divide by the number of items: X̄ = Σx ÷ N. Example: 50 marks scored by 10 students gives a mean of 5.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

or.q: What is a discrete series? Give an example.
or.answer:
A discrete series shows exact (separate) values of a variable with their frequencies.
Example: marks 30, 40, 50, 60, 70 with 4, 6, 10, 20, 10 students.
It is used for discrete variables such as the number of children per family.

questions.q: What is central tendency? State two precautions in using the arithmetic mean.
questions.answer:
Central tendency is the tendency of data to cluster around a central value, measured by an average.
Precautions: (1) The mean is a theoretical value that may not exist in fact — 2.7 children per family is impossible for any one family. (2) The mean cannot be used for qualitative data such as honesty or beauty.

questions.q: Calculate the mean: marks 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 with f = 3, 7, 8, 5, 3, 4.
Calculate the mean (discrete, short-cut): children 0–6 with families 13, 17, 20, 40, 20, 17, 13.
